prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "dalledress", with the standing line "A desktop studio that turns a seed phrase and a named series into prompts, generated images, and saved metadata." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A left-to-right bench machine. At left, a small card holds typed seed text and a series tag; a background chooser dial sits under it. A feeder arm reaches up into a rack of thirteen labelled card-drawers and pulls one card from each. The cards drop into a long assembly trough where they lock into a written prompt strip. The strip passes a side burner that rewrites it longer, then enters a boxed sender that waits, then returns a framed picture on a belt. A stencil arm lays lettering across the picture's lower edge. A thin return line loops from the finished picture back to the card rack.

Magnified circles set beside it show circle one — a single drawer card showing one word chosen by row number out of many rows. circle two — two sealed archives being weighed against a stored fingerprint, the unmatched one triggering a rebuilt cache. circle three — the phase meter face, one needle for the whole run, a second for the current step.

Colour is used so that Warm ochre marks anything the user types or chooses. Deep teal marks machine steps that call out to the image provider. Muted red marks a failed or cached run.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 13 word databases feeding one prompt; 5 pipeline stages from selection to annotation; 6 selectable image models; 5 views; 6 exported text files per image.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: series, suffix, purpose, colorLimit, backstyle, seed, enhance, annotate, nouns, adjectives, backstyles, compositions, generated, annotated, metadata, gpt-image-2, databases.tar.gz, series.tar.gz, user-series/, make build-db, Cmd+R.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: seed text, series, backstyle, base prompts, enhance prompt, image wait, download, annotate, force rerun. nouns, row index, archive hash, cache rebuild, phase meter. Dashboard, Images, Series, Databases, Settings. generated, annotated, metadata, export text, title prompt, terse prompt. suffix, purpose, colorLimit, built-in, user-series/, hidden.

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Seed normalizes before any prompt is built; Enhancement is optional; annotation needs an image. Thirteen drawers, one record drawn from each; A changed fingerprint rebuilds the cache silently. Cmd+R refreshes whichever view is open. Metadata records every record chosen; Cached runs reuse artifacts instead of paying again. Built-in series are read-only; user copies shadow them.
